title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
tagline: Linear algebra, calculus, probability, information theory and optimisation for machine learning
summary: Machine learning is applied mathematics. This course collects the linear algebra, multivariable calculus, probability, information theory and optimisation that the rest of the atlas uses, always with an eye on how they appear inside neural networks and language models.

chapters.title: Vectors, matrices and tensors
chapters.summary: Vectors and matrices as data, matrix multiplication as composition, tensors and their shapes, and what linear algebra costs on hardware.

chapters.title: Eigenvalues, SVD and low rank
chapters.summary: Eigendecompositions, the singular value decomposition, low-rank approximation and why weight matrices can be compressed.

chapters.title: Gradients and the chain rule
chapters.summary: Partial derivatives, gradients and Jacobians, the multivariable chain rule and identities of matrix calculus.

chapters.title: Probability for machine learning
chapters.summary: Random variables, common distributions, expectation, conditional probability, Bayes’ rule and sampling.

chapters.title: Estimation and likelihood
chapters.summary: Maximum likelihood and maximum a posteriori estimation, bias and variance, and the statistics of evaluation.

chapters.title: Information theory
chapters.summary: Entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence and mutual information, and why language models minimise cross-entropy.

chapters.title: Optimisation
chapters.summary: Convexity, gradient descent and its convergence, stochastic gradients, momentum and constrained optimisation.
